verdict.rationale: Sandbox0's first-party docs describe templates as reusable sandbox blueprints that define the image, resources, environment, metadata and default network policy. They also say the platform accepts public and team-scoped private container images, and that the `s0` CLI handles image build/push and template updates in CI. Both halves of the story (custom templates and bring-your-own image) are directly documented. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, deeper documentation of the template authoring/image build workflow and any image constraints.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define custom sandbox templates or bring my own container image

citations.quote: A template is the reusable blueprint for a sandbox. It defines the image, default resources, environment, metadata, and default network policy.
Sandbox0 accepts public images and team-scoped private images and imports their RootFS into the regional block store before runtime use.
GitHub Actions can run `s0` non-interactively for common Sandbox0 automation flows such as image build/push, template updates, and sandbox orchestration.
